reply_text:
I found two candidates for 2015, both in one MIT Technology Review article published on 6 August 2015. Neither is in LeCun's own writing or a full transcript.

**1. Deep learning will win at language "within a year or two."** The article quotes him saying the field is at "the same phenomenon that we were observing just before 2012," and then: "Within a year or two it will be the end." These are his words in quotation marks, but they reached me through a reporter's article rather than a transcript. From the context, "the end" means the end of doubt from researchers using older methods. The reporter introduces it as LeCun's expectation that anyone doubting deep learning's ability to master language "will be proved wrong even sooner."

**2. Virtual helpers with strong language skills in two to five years.** This one is the reporter's paraphrase, not a quotation: "LeCun guesses that virtual helpers with a mastery of language unprecedented for software will be available in just two to five years." The dated span rests only on the reporter's wording.

**Left out:**
- **Journal du Net (2 July 2015, printed Q&A in French).** The interviewer asked what AI could do "dans 10 ou 15 ans" ("in 10 or 15 years"). LeCun answered that his team was not sure it could build intelligent agents that would become digital companions. The date is in the question, not his answer, so I left it out. Your checker may want to judge it.
- **IEEE Spectrum Q&A (18 February 2015).** The page I opened cuts off partway through, before the section on the Singularity. I couldn't read the rest, so I can't say whether it holds a dated prediction. A second try at the same page cut off at the same point.
- **Popular Science (22 September 2015)** had no dated prediction from LeCun. The only dated forecast there, that Facebook's M assistant might wait on hold for users within three years, came from Alex LeBrun, not LeCun.
- **NIPS 2015 symposium (December).** A conference attendee's blog post describes LeCun comparing the road to general AI with crossing mountains in fog: some peaks are visible and an unknown number are hidden. It gives no timeline.

None of the three fixed searches turned up anything from 2015. I used all 12 searches and opened 6 pages; one search result also carried an older LeCun talk, from 2014. Nothing about when AGI or superintelligence would arrive came up for 2015, so the undated list is empty.
